First proof<PROOFARGEND_0001>Using Lemma <REF_0001> and
Modules, Lemma <REF_0002>
we see that the functor <MATH_0001> can be viewed
as <MATH_0002> for a morphism <MATH_0003> of ringed spaces.
And pulling back modules commutes with tensor constructions by
Modules, Lemmas <REF_0003>
and <REF_0004>.
The morphism <MATH_0004> is
flat for example because the stalks of <MATH_0005> are
localizations of <MATH_0006> (Lemma <REF_0005>)
and hence flat over <MATH_0007>. Thus pullback by <MATH_0008> commutes
with internal hom if the first module is finitely presented by
Modules, Lemma <REF_0006>.

Second proof<PROOFARGEND_0001>Proof of (1). By Lemma <REF_0001> to give a map
<MATH_0001> into
<MATH_0002>
we have to give a map on global sections
<MATH_0003>
which exists by definition of the tensor product of sheaves
of modules. To see that this map is an isomorphism it
suffices to check that it is an isomorphism on stalks.
And this follows from the description of the stalks
of <MATH_0004> (either in Lemma <REF_0002> or in
Modules, Lemma <REF_0003>),
the fact that tensor product commutes with localization
(Algebra, Lemma <REF_0004>) and
Modules, Lemma <REF_0005>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Proof of (2). This is similar to the proof of (1), using
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0006> and
Modules, Lemma <REF_0007>.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Proof of (3). Since the construction <MATH_0005> is functorial
there is an <MATH_0006>-linear map
<MATH_0007>.
The target of this map is the global sections of
<MATH_0008>.
Hence by Lemma <REF_0008> we obtain a map
of <MATH_0009>-modules <MATH_0010>.
We check that this is an isomorphism by comparing stalks.
If <MATH_0011> is finitely presented as an <MATH_0012>-module
then <MATH_0013> has a global finite presentation as an
<MATH_0014>-module. Hence we conclude using
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0009> and
Modules, Lemma <REF_0010>.
